This walkthrough runs the everyday loop from R: initialize a project, add a
file and commit its metadata to git, check its status, delete it, then get it
back. It is the "I re-cloned a project and need its data" sequence. The [CLI walkthrough](getting-started-cli.html)
covers the same steps from the terminal.

## Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
options(width = 1000)
library(dvs)
library(here)
```

Create a project directory and a sibling storage directory, then save R's
built-in `Theoph` dataset as a CSV.

```{r}
storage     <- basename(tempfile(fileext = "_storage"))
new_project <- basename(tempfile(fileext = "_project"))
dir.create(here::here(storage))
dir.create(here::here(new_project))
dir.create(here::here(new_project, "data"))
write.csv(Theoph, here::here(new_project, "data/theoph.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 1. Initialize

Point storage at the sibling directory. See [dvs_init()](r-init.html) for every
parameter.

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
dvs_init(here::here(storage))
```

Make the project folder a git repository before the first add. This
walkthrough uses [gert](https://docs.ropensci.org/gert/), which is installed
with usethis. `git init` in a terminal does the same.

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
gert::git_init()
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# The rendered page commits as a placeholder user. Yours is your git config.
setwd(here::here(new_project))
gert::git_config_set("user.name", "dvs docs")
gert::git_config_set("user.email", "docs@example.com")
```

::: {.callout-important}
dvs keeps the data out of git with `.gitignore` entries that it writes during
`dvs_add()`, and only when the project folder itself holds the `.git` folder.
A dvs project in a subfolder of a git repository gets no entries, and neither
does a file added before `git init`. git then sees the data. Before your first
commit, check what git would commit, as in step 2.
:::

## 2. Add and commit

Track the CSV with a message. See [dvs_add()](r-add.html).

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
dvs_add("data/theoph.csv", message = "initial Theoph data")
```

Stage the project and list what git would commit:

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
invisible(gert::git_add("."))
gert::git_status()
```

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `dvs.toml` | The project configuration: where the storage is. |
| `.dvs/data/theoph.csv.dvs` | The meta file: hash, size, who added the file, when, and the message. |
| `data/.gitignore` | The entry `/theoph.csv`, which keeps the data out of git. |
| `.dvs/.gitignore` | The entry `/.cache`, which keeps dvs's local cache out of git. |

`data/theoph.csv` is not in the list. git ignores it:

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
gert::git_ignore_path_is_ignored("data/theoph.csv")
```

Commit. If git has no name and email for you yet, the commit stops and asks.
Set them once, with `git config --global user.name "Your Name"` and
`git config --global user.email "you@example.com"`.

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
invisible(gert::git_commit("Track data/theoph.csv with dvs"))
gert::git_ls()$path
```

In a terminal, `git add -A`, `git status --short` and `git commit` do the same.
Before you stage, `git status --short --untracked-files=all` lists the files.
Plain `git status` shows only the folders `data/` and `.dvs/`, which looks as
if the data would be committed.

Commit the meta file each time you add or update data, and push it. A clone
knows only the meta files that were committed. In a colleague's clone, a file
whose meta file you did not commit is "not tracked by dvs".

## 3. Status

The file is tracked and `current`. See [dvs_status()](r-status.html).

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
dvs_status()
```

## 4. Remove the file

Delete the local copy, the moment after a fresh clone where the data is not on
disk yet.

```{r}
unlink(here::here(new_project, "data/theoph.csv"))
```

## 5. Status again

The file is now `absent`: tracked, but missing locally.

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
dvs_status()
```

::: {.callout-note}
dvs reports five statuses: `current`, `absent`, `stale` (unchanged since dvs
wrote it, while the tracked version moved on), `modified` (edited locally) and
`unsynced` (different, with no record of what dvs wrote). See
[dvs_status()](r-status.html) and [Storage and meta files](intro-internals.html).
:::

## 6. Get

Restore the file from storage. See [dvs_get()](r-get.html).

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
dvs_get("data/theoph.csv")
```

## 7. Status again

The file is `current` again. The loop is complete.

```{r}
setwd(here::here(new_project))
dvs_status()
```

## Cleanup

```{r}
unlink(here::here(new_project), recursive = TRUE)
unlink(here::here(storage),     recursive = TRUE)
```
